clue.text: Churchman around North missing old car

indicators.note: missing tells us the letters for 'around' and 'North' are taken out of the churchman

parts.note: a churchman can be an Anglican, a member of the Church of England
C, short for circa, means around

explanation.surface: A clergyman out driving finds his vintage motor is lost somewhere up north.
explanation.walkthrough: The C and N come out of different places in ANGLICAN, in the same order as the clue gives them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ford Anglia was a British family car, made from the 1940s to 1960s, so it is an old model.

clue.text: Money once bottled by Marilyn in recession

indicators.note: a recession is a going back, so the letters found are read backwards
something bottled by a word is held inside it, so we look for letters inside the name

explanation.surface: Marilyn Monroe hoarding her old cash in jars during an economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in recession' looks like economics, but it turns ARIL (found inside 'Marilyn') back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: The lira was the Italian currency before the euro replaced it, so it was money in the past.

clue.text: Street worker hiding something fishy? He might be a forger

indicators.note: one thing hiding another keeps it covered inside, so the fishy item sits within the other letters

parts.note: a man is a worker, as in a hired hand
an eel is a fish, so literally something fishy

explanation.surface: A street labourer concealing a dodgy item might be a counterfeiter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forger' suggests a fraudster, but here it means someone who forges metal; 'something fishy' suggests a scam but is simply a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker in the steel industry may well forge metal, so he is a forger in the smithy sense, not the fraud sense.

clue.text: Sort of transfer that's concerning inside club

indicators.note: inside places the word for 'concerning' within the word for 'club'

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club
on means concerning, as in a talk on politics

explanation.surface: A football transfer deal said to involve someone inside the club.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron-on transfer is a design applied to fabric using the heat of an iron, so it is one kind of transfer.

clue.text: Scotsman heading for Tyrol picked up skiing guide?

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: Rab is a typical Scottish man's name, short for Robert

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, so we take the start of the place name

explanation.surface: A Scot bound for the Austrian Alps collects a ski instructor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' looks like a pick-up or a sound clue, but in a down answer it turns RAB plus T upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-bar is a ski lift that pulls skiers uphill, so with the question mark it is a playful guide for skiers.

clue.text: 24 caught leaving cocaine around central party

indicators.note: around has the shortened drug word wrapped about the next pieces
leaving means the letter for 'caught' departs from the drug's slang name

parts.note: coke is slang for cocaine
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
key means central or crucial
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A user, caught at the heart of a party, giving up the drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 refers to the answer at 24-across, meaning uninjured or fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal expressions of agreement or being fine, so the cross-reference is a synonym.

clue.text: Anger's reasonable during test

indicators.note: during puts the word for 'reasonable' within the word for 'test'

parts.note: to prove is to test, as in the proof of the pudding
OK means reasonable or acceptable

explanation.surface: Someone's temper being tolerable in the middle of an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: To provoke someone is to anger or incite them, a straightforward synonym for the verb.

clue.text: Joking about crime that's overcome security feature

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the joking word goes round the other piece

parts.note: banter is joking talk

indicators.note: something overcome is turned over, so the word for crime is flipped

parts.note: sin is a wrong or crime

explanation.surface: Light-hearted chat about a crime that someone has got over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's overcome' reads as a crime got over, but it signals turning the word upside down. The answer is the double-N spelling of banister.
explanation.definitionFit: A banister, also spelt with a double N, is the handrail on a staircase, which keeps people from falling.

clue.text: Minimal clothing, good for one's sporting activity

indicators.note: good for one means the letter for good takes the place of the letter for one

parts.note: a bikini is a very skimpy swimsuit
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Skimpy clothing that is fine for a person taking part in sport.
explanation.walkthrough: The swap is made on the final I of BIKINI.
explanation.definitionFit: Cycling for sport or leisure is a sporting activity, so the riding of bikes fits it as an example.

clue.text: Madeleine might be seen at this retailer

definitions.text: Madeleine might be seen at this retailer

parts.words: Madeleine might be seen at this retailer
parts.note: Madeleine reads as a woman's name, but a madeleine is a small French sponge cake sold in a bread shop

explanation.surface: A woman called Madeleine spotted at a particular shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A madeleine is a small shell-shaped cake, the kind of thing on sale where bread and cakes are made.

clue.text: Butcher shortened venture somewhere in Ireland

indicators.note: shortened means the word for butcher loses its last letter

parts.note: to butcher is to kill
to dare is to venture or risk

explanation.surface: A butcher cutting back on a risky business deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Kildare is a county and town in Ireland, so it is one place there.

clue.text: Dancer to watch Classical figure after career possibly over

indicators.note: after places the watching and figure pieces following the reversed run
over means turned over, so the word for career is reversed

parts.note: to career is to run headlong, so run is an example
to eye is to watch
V is five in Roman numerals, a figure from Classical times

explanation.surface: A dancer looks at a statue of antiquity once his career might be finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classical figure' sounds like a statue but is a Roman numeral; 'career' is the verb meaning rush.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Nureyev was a celebrated Soviet-born ballet star, so he is an example of a dancer.

clue.text: Northern aristocrat many suspect to be an underachiever?

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious or unsound, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A northern noble whom plenty of people believe to be a failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' reads as a verb but works as an anagram signal on MANY.
explanation.definitionFit: A nearly man is someone who keeps almost succeeding but never quite wins, so with the question mark he underachieves.

clue.text: Quay providing shelter around mid-section of Severn

indicators.note: around has the shelter word wrapped about the middle letters

parts.note: lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

indicators.note: the mid-section of a word is its central letters

explanation.surface: A wharf offering cover beside the middle stretch of the River Severn.
explanation.walkthrough: The Severn is Britain's longest river; only its central two letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: A levee is an embankment along a river, and also a landing place, so it serves as a quay.

clue.text: The ultimate of companies acquired by Mark. Enterprise propels him

indicators.note: acquired by tells us that letter is taken on by the mark word, joined to its front
the ultimate of a word is its final letter

parts.note: a pock is a mark or scar on the skin

explanation.surface: A firm taken over by a man named Mark, whose business drives him on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enterprise' looks like business, but it is the starship Enterprise from Star Trek.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Spock is the science officer carried through space aboard the starship Enterprise in Star Trek.

clue.text: Idle creature getting mum to carry large amount

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it, so the quiet word holds the amount word

parts.note: mum means silent, and SH is a call for silence
a lot is a large amount

explanation.surface: A lazy animal persuading its mother to bear a heavy load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like mother, but it means quiet, giving SH.
explanation.definitionFit: The sloth is a slow-moving tree-dwelling animal famed for laziness, so it is an idle creature.

clue.text: Explorer's daily bread added to weight

indicators.note: added to puts the weight word on after the livelihood word

parts.note: one's daily bread is one's living or livelihood
a stone is a unit of weight, fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: An adventurer's food for the day being put on top of the scales.
explanation.definitionFit: David Livingstone was a Scottish missionary who travelled through Africa, so he is a famous example of an explorer.

clue.text: Gradually approach field exercises wearing brace

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow or field

indicators.note: something wearing a garment is inside it, so the exercises sit within the pair

parts.note: a brace is a pair, a duo
PT is physical training, school exercises

explanation.surface: Drills in a meadow while wearing a back brace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brace' looks like a support worn on the body, but it means a pair, as in a brace of pheasants.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead up to something is to work towards it step by step, an idiom for a gradual approach.

clue.text: Ancient Greek boxes well at first

indicators.note: at first puts the word for well at the very start

parts.note: so is used like well to begin a remark
crates are boxes

explanation.surface: An old Greek man boxing skilfully to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' reads as a verb about fighting but is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Socrates was the Athenian philosopher of the fifth century BC, so he is an example of an ancient Greek.

clue.text: One's learned in time to raise the surface level

indicators.note: in places the graduate within the word for time

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
a grad, a graduate, is one who is learned

explanation.surface: A person studies over time to lift the level of the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: In geology, to aggrade is to build up a riverbed or land surface by depositing sediment, raising its height.

clue.text: Rest ordered, following backing of nurse

indicators.note: following puts the rearranged rest after the turned little word
backing means the little word is turned back to front
ordered means arranged, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A patient told to rest after a nurse's support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support but reverses OF to FO; 'ordered' rearranges REST into STER.
explanation.definitionFit: To foster is to nurse or nurture, such as caring for a child or encouraging an idea.

clue.text: Good people showing kindness

parts.note: a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: Decent folk being generous to others.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace can mean goodwill or favour freely shown, a synonym for kindness.

clue.text: Tea sustains one on computer before getting to another beverage

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the tea piece follows the computer
before getting puts the tea piece ahead of the final word

parts.note: a Mac is an Apple computer

indicators.note: to sustain is to hold up, so the tea word holds the letter for one

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Tea keeping a person going at the computer before moving on to another drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another beverage' refers back to 'Tea': the answer is a different drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A macchiato is an espresso marked with a dash of milk, so it is a drink other than tea.

clue.text: Tweeter hurt by something in circulation

parts.note: to mar is to damage or hurt
tin is slang for money, which is in circulation

explanation.surface: A social media poster wounded by a rumour doing the rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tweeter' suggests social media, but it means a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The martin is a small swallow-like bird, and birds tweet, so it is a playful word for a bird.

clue.text: Some eating pith, not one being apprehensive

indicators.note: eating puts the reduced pith word inside the word for some

parts.note: any means some, as in have you any?

indicators.note: not means the letter for one is left out

parts.note: the gist is the pith or core of a matter
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Some people eating orange pith, but one nervous person declining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pith' suggests orange peel, but here it means the core of an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling angst means feeling anxious dread, so the informal adjective describes someone worried or nervous.

clue.text: Lady's applying much make-up with greater severity

indicators.note: applying puts the make-up piece on before the lady's piece
much of a word means most of it, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: rouge is red make-up for the cheeks
her is the possessive for a woman, a lady's

explanation.surface: A woman plastering on the cosmetics with a heavier hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Rougher as an adverb means more harshly, so it says with more severity.

clue.text: Legendary captain's stroke at Lord's?

definitions.meaning: Captain ... is the pirate villain in Peter Pan
in cricket; Lord's is the famous London cricket ground

explanation.surface: A famed skipper's shot at the home of cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The pirate of Peter Pan is a fictional captain, and the cricket shot of that name is a stroke.

clue.text: A pair of hands uninjured

parts.note: the two hands are the left (L) and the right

explanation.surface: A set of workers who came through unscathed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pair of hands' suggests workers, but it means left and right.
explanation.definitionFit: Being all right means being safe and unharmed, a synonym for uninjured.

clue.text: Tool starts to rust (always kept externally)

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A garden implement begins to corrode when it is always left outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' looks like the verb begin, but it picks the first letters of the next four words.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a long-handled garden implement with teeth, used for gathering leaves.

clue.text: Likewise, advisor regularly devours Times

indicators.note: devours means the picked letters swallow up the times piece
regularly means taking every other letter of the word

parts.note: T stands for time, so times is two Ts

explanation.surface: Similarly, a consultant routinely reads through the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper, but it gives T twice; the even letters of 'advisor' are DIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto means the same again, used to say the same goes for this one too.

clue.text: Dean, say, organised rite including church music

indicators.note: including puts the church and music pieces inside the rearranged letters
organised means arranged, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
ska is a Jamaican music style

explanation.surface: A cathedral dean has arranged a service that includes some sacred music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dean' looks like a cleric, but it is Christopher Dean, the British Olympic ice dancer; 'organised' rearranges RITE into ITER.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Dean won Olympic gold on ice with Jayne Torvill, so he is an example of a skater.
